title: NSGo game project (version 1)
description: File is the root of a versioned game.yaml project file.

version.description: Version is the schema version; it must equal CurrentVersion (1).

name.description: Name is the game's display name, which nsgo.yaml's name follows.

id.description: ID is the game's reverse-DNS application identifier, such as dev.nsgo.game.examples.caverun, which nsgo.yaml's id follows.

appVersion.description: AppVersion is the game's release version, such as 0.1.0, which nsgo.yaml's version follows.

window.description: Window is the main window's size, limits, title and appearance.

display.description: Display is the virtual resolution the game draws at; nil draws at the window's own size.

input.description: Input is the input map bound into an input.Actions; nil binds nothing.

audio.description: Audio holds the master volume and the audio buses a sound.Mixer is configured with; nil configures nothing.

physics.description: Physics holds the default 2D and 3D gravity, solver iterations and named collision layers shared by scenes; nil uses each engine's defaults.

autoload.description: Autoload lists the scenes and resources loaded at startup; nil loads nothing.

export.description: Export holds the build output directory and the export presets per platform, which nsgo.yaml's build section follows; nil leaves nsgo.yaml without them.

editor.description: Editor holds the scene editor's settings for this project; nil uses its defaults.

assets.description: Assets declares the atlases, textures, audio, fonts, models and asset manifest game assets builds; nil declares none.

navigation.description: Navigation holds the settings and agent types game navmesh bakes a scene's navigation meshes with (see the navbake3d package); nil bakes one agent type called DefaultNavAgent with the default settings.

packs.description: Packs records the library packs installed into the project, in the order they were first installed: the files each wrote and the autoload entries and editor plugins each added, so that a later install of the pack can update it and a removal can undo it (see the tooling/library package). nil records none.

Action.description: Action is one named action and the physical inputs that trigger it.

bindings.description: Bindings are the inputs that press the action; an action without any is declared for code to bind, such as one an axis reads.

assist.description: Assist declares which player motor assists (hold-to-toggle, mash-to-hold) apply to this action; nil leaves the action ineligible so menu actions are never latched.

ActionAssist.description: ActionAssist declares which player motor assists an action opts into.

toggle.description: Toggle reports whether a player may latch this action on press and release it on the next press.

mash.description: Mash reports whether a player may satisfy rapid-press mashing of this action by holding it.

mashRate.description: MashRate is the synthetic press rate in presses per second used when MashToHold is active; 0 uses input.DefaultMashRate (10). Refused when Mash is false.

Assets.description: Assets declares the targets game assets builds: the sprite atlases to pack, the textures to encode, the audio to convert, the fonts to bake, the models to pack and the asset manifest to generate. Paths in it are slash-separated and relative to the project root, and may not leave it.

cache.description: Cache is the build cache's path; empty is DefaultAssetsCache.

atlases.description: Atlases are the sprite atlases to pack, each from one folder of PNG images.

textures.description: Textures are the images to encode into KTX2 containers.

audio.description: Audio are the WAV files to normalize, resample and convert.

fonts.description: Fonts are the TrueType and OpenType fonts, and the folders of PNG glyph images, to bake into bitmap fonts.

models.description: Models are the glTF models to pack into single GLB files.

manifest.description: Manifest, when set, is the typed Go asset manifest generated after every other target is built.

remote.description: Remote, when set, copies loose assets to content-hashed filenames (<name>.<hash8>.<ext>) under its out folder and writes remote.yaml for CDN hosting.

AtlasTarget.description: AtlasTarget is one sprite atlas packed from a folder of PNG images, as game pack packs it.

name.description: Name is the base name of the atlas's page files, such as "ui" for ui.png and ui.json.

in.description: In is the folder of PNG images, searched recursively.

out.description: Out is the folder the pages are written to.

padding.description: Padding is the transparent gap between frames in pixels; nil is 1.

extrude.description: Extrude is how many edge pixels are repeated around each frame.

maxWidth.description: MaxWidth bounds a page's width in pixels; 0 is 2048.

maxHeight.description: MaxHeight bounds a page's height in pixels; 0 is 2048.

scale.description: Scale is written to the pages' meta.scale; 0 is 1.

trim.description: Trim removes transparent borders around each image; nil is true.

Audio.description: Audio is the master volume, global voice budget, buses (sound.Mixer groups), concurrency groups, and bus ducking rules a game plays through.

master.description: Master is the default master volume in [0, 1]; nil leaves it at 1.

maxVoices.description: MaxVoices is the mixer's global concurrent voice budget; 0 uses sound.DefaultMaxVoices.

buses.description: Buses are the mixer groups in declaration order.

concurrency.description: Concurrency lists shared concurrency groups limiting and resolving overlapping voices across sounds.

duck.description: Duck lists bus ducking rules that lower one bus while another bus or concurrency group plays.

AudioDuck.description: AudioDuck configures ducking reduction and attack/release envelope timing for a concurrency group.

amount.description: Amount is the volume reduction fraction in [0, 1] (0 disables ducking, 0.4 lowers by 40%, 1 silences).

attack.description: Attack is how quickly ducking ramps in; 0 applies immediately.

release.description: Release is how quickly volume recovers; 0 restores immediately.

AudioTarget.description: AudioTarget is one WAV file normalized, resampled and converted, as game audio converts it.

in.description: In is the source WAV file.

format.description: Format is one of AudioFormats; empty is wav. aac and mp3 need an external encoder, as game audio describes.

rate.description: Rate is the sample rate in Hz; 0 keeps the input's.

channels.description: Channels is 1 for mono or 2 for stereo; 0 keeps the input's.

peakDB.description: PeakDB normalizes the peak to this level in dBFS; it may not be set with RMSDB.

rmsDB.description: RMSDB normalizes the loudness to this level in dBFS with soft clipping; it may not be set with PeakDB.

bitrate.description: Bitrate is the AAC or MP3 bitrate in kbps; 0 is 128.

Autoload.description: Autoload lists the scenes and resources a game loads at startup.

mainScene.description: MainScene names the scene in Scenes the game starts in; empty leaves the choice to the game.

scenes.description: Scenes are sceneformat YAML documents, loaded and validated at startup.

resources.description: Resources are other files loaded as bytes at startup, such as data tables.

Axis.description: Axis is a named axis over two actions, as input.Actions.BindAxis binds it.

negative.description: Negative names a declared action that drives the axis toward -1; at least one of Negative and Positive is required.

positive.description: Positive names a declared action that drives the axis toward +1; at least one of Negative and Positive is required.

Binding.description: Binding is one physical input bound to an action.

kind.description: Kind is KindTouchRegion, KindMouseButton, KindMouseRegion, KindKey, KindKeyCode or KindGamepadButton.

button.description: Button is a mouse button ("left", "right", "middle", "back" or "forward") for KindMouseButton and KindMouseRegion, or a standard gamepad button (one of GamepadButtons) for KindGamepadButton; refused by other kinds.

key.description: Key is the keyboard key name (such as "a", "space", "left", "enter" or "shift") for KindKey, matched case-insensitively as input.Key does; refused by other kinds.

code.description: Code is the physical keyboard position (such as "KeyW", "ArrowLeft", "Space" or "ShiftLeft") for KindKeyCode, as input.KeyCode reads it; refused by other kinds.

region.description: Region is the rectangle in virtual coordinates (or view coordinates without a Display) that KindTouchRegion and KindMouseRegion test; refused by other kinds.

Bitcrush.description: Bitcrush is a lo-fi quantizer (sound.Bitcrush): Bits in [1, 15] and Downsample 0 or more, where 0 and 1 keep every frame.

bits.description: Bits is the quantized bit depth in [1, 15].

downsample.description: Downsample holds each sample for this many frames; 0 and 1 keep every frame.

Budgets.description: Budgets holds release size and performance thresholds checked against each built package.

qualityProfile.description: QualityProfile names the quality preset frameTimeP95Ms is measured at (for example "low", "medium", or "high"); empty defaults to "low".

downloadSizeMB.description: DownloadSizeMB is the maximum acceptable release download size in megabytes; 0 leaves it unset.

frameTimeP95Ms.description: FrameTimeP95Ms is the maximum acceptable 95th-percentile frame time in milliseconds; 0 leaves it unset.

Bus.description: Bus is one sound.Mixer group: its default volume and its DSP effect chain.

name.description: Name is the mixer group, such as "music" or "sfx".

volume.description: Volume is the default volume in [0, 1] until the player sets one; nil leaves it at 1.

effects.description: Effects is the bus's DSP chain, applied in order.

BusDuck.description: BusDuck lowers one mixer bus while another bus or concurrency group has active sounds.

bus.description: Bus is the mixer bus whose volume is lowered.

by.description: By is the triggering mixer bus or concurrency group name.

amount.description: Amount is the volume reduction fraction in [0, 1] (0 disables ducking, 0.4 lowers by 40%, 1 silences).

attack.description: Attack is how quickly bus fades down when by starts playing; 0 applies immediately.

release.description: Release is how quickly bus recovers once by finishes playing; 0 restores immediately.

ConcurrencyGroup.description: ConcurrencyGroup defines a shared voice concurrency group under audio.concurrency.

name.description: Name is the unique concurrency group name referenced by sounds.

max.description: Max is the maximum simultaneous active voices in this group (or per owner when scope is owner); 0 imposes no group cap.

resolve.description: Resolve chooses which voice is dropped when max is reached: refuse (default), oldest, farthest, quietest, or lowestPriority.

scope.description: Scope chooses whether max, retrigger, and duck apply across the whole group ("global", default) or per sound owner ("owner").

retrigger.description: Retrigger is the minimum duration between accepted voice starts in this group (or owner).

stealFade.description: StealFade is the fade-out duration applied to voices stolen by this group's resolution rule.

duck.description: Duck lowers older active voices in the same concurrency scope while newer voices play.

Delay.description: Delay is a feedback delay line (sound.Delay).

time.description: Time is the echo spacing, such as 250ms; it must be positive.

feedback.description: Feedback is the feedback gain in [0, 0.99].

wet.description: Wet is the wet mix level in [0, 1].

Display.description: Display is the virtual resolution a screen.Viewport maps onto the window.

width.description: Width is the virtual canvas width in game points; it must be positive.

height.description: Height is the virtual canvas height in game points; it must be positive.

mode.description: Mode is how the canvas fits a window of another aspect ratio: "fit" (the default when empty), "fill", "stretch" or "expand", as screen.Mode names them.

integerScale.description: IntegerScale scales by whole multiples only, as screen.Viewport.IntegerScale does.

pixelSnap.description: PixelSnap aligns the canvas to whole points, as screen.Viewport.PixelSnap does.

barColor.description: BarColor is the CSS color of letterbox and pillarbox bars, parsed with core.ParseColor; empty is opaque black.

Editor.description: Editor is the scene editor's settings for one project.

plugins.description: Plugins names the editor plugins the scene editor turns on for this project, in the order their panels and tools appear. A plugin is Go code built into the editor binary (editor.Plugin), so this list only turns plugins on; each name is unique and has no spaces or control characters.

Effect.description: Effect is one DSP effect on a bus; exactly one field must be set.

lowPass.description: LowPass is a biquad low-pass filter.

highPass.description: HighPass is a biquad high-pass filter.

delay.description: Delay is a feedback delay line.

gain.description: Gain scales every sample by a non-negative factor.

bitcrush.description: Bitcrush quantizes bit depth and sample rate.

name.description: Name uniquely identifies the entry within its list.

path.description: Path is the file's slash-separated path relative to the project root, as fs.ValidPath accepts it.

Export.description: Export holds the build output directory, optional release budgets, and one export preset per platform.

output.description: Output is the directory builds are written to; empty is NSGo's default (dist).

budgets.description: Budgets are optional release thresholds checked before and after each build (download size and frame time p95 at a quality profile).

presets.description: Presets are the platforms the game exports to, in build order.

Filter.description: Filter is a biquad low-pass or high-pass filter (sound.LowPass, sound.HighPass).

cutoffHz.description: CutoffHz is the cutoff frequency in hertz; it must be positive.

q.description: Q is the filter's quality factor; 0 is Butterworth.

FontTarget.description: FontTarget is one TrueType or OpenType font, or one folder of PNG glyph images, baked into an AngelCode BMFont, which text.LoadBMFont reads: a text .fnt file and the PNG pages its glyphs are packed on, named after it, such as hud.png beside hud.fnt, or hud-0.png, hud-1.png and so on when the glyphs need several pages.

in.description: In is the .ttf or .otf font file, or a folder of PNG glyph images when the path has no .ttf or .otf extension.

out.description: Out is the .fnt file written; the pages are written beside it.

size.description: Size is the font size in pixels the glyphs are drawn at; 0 is DefaultFontSize. A folder of glyph images keeps its images' pixels instead.

chars.description: Chars are the characters baked, each once, in any order; empty is DefaultFontChars. A character the font has no glyph for is left out. A folder of glyph images bakes every image it holds instead.

padding.description: Padding is the transparent gap around each glyph on the pages in pixels; nil is 1.

glyphs.description: Glyphs maps a glyph image's slash-separated path relative to In to the character it draws, for images whose base name's stem is not one character, such as "plus.png": "+". A folder input only takes it.

spacing.description: Spacing is the extra advance in pixels after each glyph of a folder input.

align.description: Align is where each glyph of a folder input sits in the line: "top", "center" or "bottom"; empty is "bottom".

Gain.description: Gain scales every sample by Factor (sound.Gain), which must be finite and non-negative.

factor.description: Factor is the non-negative linear gain multiplier.

GamepadAxis.description: GamepadAxis is a named axis read from a connected game controller's analog stick, as input.Actions.BindGamepadAxis binds it.

name.description: Name uniquely identifies the gamepad axis.

deadZone.description: DeadZone is the stick deflection below which the axis reads 0, strictly less than 1; 0 uses input.DefaultGamepadDeadZone and a negative value turns the dead zone off.

axial.description: Axial applies DeadZone to this axis alone instead of radially over both axes of the stick.

sensitivity.description: Sensitivity multiplies the dead-zoned reading before clamping to [-1, 1]; 0 uses 1.

invert.description: Invert negates the resulting axis value.

Input.description: Input is a game's input map: named actions with their physical bindings, axes over pairs of actions, device motion axes and game controller stick axes.

actions.description: Actions are the named actions in the order they are declared.

axes.description: Axes are the named axes, each reading -1 for its negative action and +1 for its positive one.

motionAxes.description: MotionAxes are the named axes read from the device's tilt and gyroscope.

gamepadAxes.description: GamepadAxes are the named axes read from a connected game controller's analog sticks.

LDtkIntGridRule.description: LDtkIntGridRule maps one LDtk IntGrid value (by identifier/group name or positive numeric value) to tile collision flags. Exactly one of Name or Value must be set; leaving Solid, OneWay, and Flags all unset explicitly maps matching cells to 0 (non-colliding).

name.description: Name matches an LDtk IntGrid value identifier or IntGrid value group identifier (case-insensitive).

value.description: Value matches a positive numeric LDtk IntGrid value (1, 2, ...).

solid.description: Solid sets tilemap.TileSolid on matching IntGrid cells.

oneWay.description: OneWay sets tilemap.TileOneWay on matching IntGrid cells.

flags.description: Flags sets additional game-defined tilemap.TileFlags bits on matching IntGrid cells alongside Solid and OneWay.

ManifestTarget.description: ManifestTarget is the typed Go asset manifest generated from a folder of assets, as game manifest generates it.

in.description: In is the assets folder scanned.

package.description: Package is the generated file's package name; empty is "assets".

prefix.description: Prefix is prepended to each asset's path to form its URI; empty is "asset:".

embed.description: Embed emits //go:embed directives instead of URI references.

embedDir.description: EmbedDir is prepended to the //go:embed patterns.

ModelTarget.description: ModelTarget is one glTF model packed into a single binary glTF (.glb) file: its buffers merged into the file's binary chunk and the images it references by file embedded, so the game loads one file.

in.description: In is the .gltf or .glb file; the buffers and images it references by relative path are read beside it.

scale.description: Scale multiplies the size of every scene of the model, such as 0.01 for a model exported in centimeters; 0 is 1.

animations.description: Animations keeps the model's animations when true and leaves them out when false; nil is true.

MotionAxis.description: MotionAxis is a named axis read from a device motion sensor, as input.Actions.BindMotionAxis binds it.

name.description: Name uniquely identifies the motion axis.

deadZone.description: DeadZone is the sensor dead zone in [0, 1); 0 takes input.MotionAxisOptions' default.

sensitivity.description: Sensitivity scales the reading; 0 takes input.MotionAxisOptions' default.

maxRange.description: MaxRange is the full-deflection sensor range; 0 takes input.MotionAxisOptions' default.

smoothing.description: Smoothing is the low-pass smoothing factor in [0, 1); 0 disables smoothing.

invert.description: Invert negates the resulting axis value.

NavAgent.description: NavAgent is one agent type navigation meshes are baked for, as navbake3d.AgentType defines it; each size 0 or omitted takes navbake3d's default.

name.description: Name uniquely identifies the agent type, such as "humanoid".

radius.description: Radius is how far the mesh keeps from walls and ledges.

height.description: Height is the clearance the agent needs.

maxSlope.description: MaxSlope is the steepest walkable slope in degrees, below 90.

maxClimb.description: MaxClimb is the highest step the agent climbs.

Navigation.description: Navigation is the navigation mesh bake settings of a project, as navbake3d.Settings defines them: each field 0 or omitted takes navbake3d's default. The scene's own layers are all baked.

cellSize.description: CellSize is the width and depth of one cell of the voxel grid the level is baked on, in world units.

cellHeight.description: CellHeight is the height of one cell, the precision of heights, clearances and steps.

minRegionArea.description: MinRegionArea is the smallest area of an island of walkable surface that is kept.

maxEdgeLength.description: MaxEdgeLength is the longest a polygon edge along a wall may be.

maxSimplificationError.description: MaxSimplificationError is the farthest a simplified outline may stray from the walkable area.

maxVertsPerPoly.description: MaxVertsPerPoly is the largest number of vertices in one polygon, from 3 to MaxNavVertsPerPoly.

detailSampleDistance.description: DetailSampleDistance is the spacing of the height samples polygons follow uneven ground with, at least CellSize.

detailSampleMaxError.description: DetailSampleMaxError is how far the polygons' triangles may stray from the sampled height.

agents.description: Agents are the agent types a scene gets a navigation mesh each for, in the order the baked file lists them; empty bakes one called DefaultNavAgent.

Pack.description: Pack is one library pack installed into the project. Its files are Dir joined with each of Files, and Scenes, Resources and Plugins name the autoload entries and editor plugins the install added, which must still be in the file; an entry or plugin the project held before the install is not the pack's and is not listed.

name.description: Name identifies the pack in its library: lower-case ASCII letters, digits and '-', starting with a letter or digit.

packVersion.description: PackVersion is the version of the pack that was installed, such as 1.2.0.

sha256.description: SHA256 is the pack's digest, 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits, which tells one release of the pack from another whatever its version says.

dir.description: Dir is the slash-separated directory inside the project the pack's files were written to.

files.description: Files are the slash-separated paths of the pack's files relative to Dir, sorted and unique.

scenes.description: Scenes names the autoload scenes the install added.

resources.description: Resources names the autoload resources the install added.

plugins.description: Plugins names the editor plugins the install turned on.

Physics.description: Physics holds the project's default 2D and 3D gravity, solver iterations, named collision layers, and LDtk IntGrid collision flag mappings shared by scenes.

gravity2D.description: Gravity2D is the 2D gravity acceleration in points per second squared (for example {y: 980} in +Y-down screen space); nil leaves 2D gravity at (0, 0).

gravity3D.description: Gravity3D is the 3D gravity acceleration in units per second squared (for example {y: -9.81} in Y-up 3D space); nil leaves 3D gravity at physics3d's default (0, -9.81, 0).

solverIterations2D.description: SolverIterations2D is the number of sequential-impulse iterations per 2D rigid step; 0 uses physics.DefaultSolverIterations.

solverIterations3D.description: SolverIterations3D is the number of solver iterations per 3D physics step; 0 uses physics3d's default.

layers.description: Layers maps human-readable collision layer names (such as "player", "walls", and "coins") to bit indices in [0, 31], in declaration order.

ldtkIntGrid.description: LDtkIntGrid maps LDtk IntGrid value identifiers, group identifiers, or numeric values to tilemap.TileFlags when loading .ldtk projects.

PhysicsLayer.description: PhysicsLayer assigns a human-readable collision layer name to a bit index in [0, 31].

name.description: Name uniquely identifies the collision layer, such as "player", "walls", or "coins".

bit.description: Bit is the collision bit index in [0, 31], matching LayerBit(Bit).

Preset.description: Preset is the export preset of one platform.

platform.description: Platform is one of Platforms, such as "web" or "macos".

targets.description: Targets are the NSGo build targets of the platform to build, such as macos_arm64; empty builds the platform name itself, which NSGo expands to its default targets.

Rect.description: Rect is an axis-aligned rectangle with a positive size.

x.description: X is the horizontal origin in virtual points.

y.description: Y is the vertical origin in virtual points.

width.description: Width is the rectangle's width in virtual points; it must be positive.

height.description: Height is the rectangle's height in virtual points; it must be positive.

RemoteTarget.description: RemoteTarget publishes loose assets into Out under content-hashed filenames (<name>.<hash8>.<ext>) and writes a remote.yaml manifest mapping each asset URI to its hashed path, byte size and SHA-256 digest.

in.description: In is the folder of assets to publish remotely; when empty, Manifest.In is used, or the outputs built by the other targets when no manifest is configured.

out.description: Out is the directory written with content-hashed files and remote.yaml, such as "dist/cdn".

base.description: Base is the default origin URL prefix written into remote.yaml, such as "https://cdn.example.com/game/".

prefix.description: Prefix is prepended to each published file's relative path to form its URI in remote.yaml; empty is "asset:".

include.description: Include, when non-empty, limits published files to those matching at least one slash-separated path prefix (ending in "/"), exact relative path, or path.Match glob pattern.

Reverb.description: Reverb is a Freeverb-style reverb (sound.Reverb); each field is in [0, 1].

roomSize.description: RoomSize controls reverb decay size in [0, 1].

wet.description: Wet is the wet mix level in [0, 1].

TextureTarget.description: TextureTarget is one PNG or JPEG image encoded into a KTX2 container, as game tex encodes it.

format.description: Format is one of TextureFormats; empty is rgba8.

mipmaps.description: Mipmaps writes the whole mipmap chain down to 1x1.

srgb.description: SRGB marks the texture sRGB and filters its mipmaps in linear light.

Vec2.description: Vec2 is a two-dimensional vector in game.yaml, such as 2D gravity.

Vec3.description: Vec3 is a three-dimensional vector in game.yaml, such as 3D gravity.

Window.description: Window is the main window's content size in points, its size limits, its title and its appearance.

title.description: Title is the window's title; empty uses File.Name.

width.description: Width is the window's starting content width in points; it must be positive.

height.description: Height is the window's starting content height in points; it must be positive.

minWidth.description: MinWidth is the smallest content width the user may resize the window to; 0 is no limit.

minHeight.description: MinHeight is the smallest content height the user may resize the window to; 0 is no limit.

maxWidth.description: MaxWidth is the largest content width the user may resize the window to; 0 is no limit.

maxHeight.description: MaxHeight is the largest content height the user may resize the window to; 0 is no limit.

resizable.description: Resizable says whether the user may resize the window; nil defaults to true.

appearance.description: Appearance starts the app "light" or "dark" whatever the system's; empty follows the system. nsgo.yaml's appearance follows it.
